ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN and 50% Rule, the South African targeted financial sanctions list under s 26A of FICA and the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004, and the FIC administrative sanctions register. PEP status determination under s 21D of FICA requires domestic and foreign prominent persons to be flagged, with enhanced due diligence and verified source-of-funds documentation. Continuous 24-hour sanctions monitoring must follow onboarding; the bank conducts confirmatory screening at LC and SWIFT account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eservices portal — https://eservices.cipc.co.za (Company Name Reservation form CoR 9.1)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in one of South Africa's 11 official languages and expressed in Latin alphabetic characters; non-Latin script names (e.g., Arabic, Cyrillic, Chinese ideographs) must be transliterated to Latin characters. Descriptive tokens must not misrepresent the activities of the company (s 11(1)-(2), Companies Act 71 of 2008), and numerals, abbreviations, and special symbols must comply with CIPC name-imaging conventions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: 1) CIPC issues a rejection notice stating the statutory ground (confusing similarity, offensive name, restricted token, or name-image non-compliance). 2) The applicant may immediately re-file a fresh CoR 9.1 with a revised name; a new statutory fee applies and there is no cooling-off period. 3) An administrative appeal may be lodged with the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 within 60 days of the rejection notification, using the prescribed CTR 160 form, where the refusal is based on confusing similarity or alleged non-compliance. 4) If the rejection arises from a CIPC data or classification error, a written objection with supporting evidence may be submitted through the CIPC digital correspondence portal for administrative correction within 10 business days. 5) If the reservation lapses or expires, the applicant must re-apply; an expired name carries no proprietary priority rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: CIPC accepts a registered-office service provider's physical street address. A pure virtual office or mailbox without on-site document reception and without a physical production footprint is not permissible for ISIC 2813 industrial manufacturing: the National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications, sectoral licensing authorities, and environmental regulators require a physical cryogenic pump manufacturing site in South Africa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 75% — industrial goods manufacturing under ISIC 2813 is exposed to unannounced inspections by the Department of Employment and Labour (OHSA and COIDA compliance), the National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications, environmental enforcement agencies under NEMA, and the corporate bank's facility-diligence visits supporting LC and SWIFT working capital lines.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 13(1), 14, 19, 66, 76 and 152; Companies Regulations 2011, Chapter 2 (regs 14-19).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A or custom MOI approved by the incorporator).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act. No escrow account is required or regulated by CIPC; the subscription price, once agreed, must be fully settled into the company's bank account and reflected in the share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the undersigned, being the sole incorporator and appointed first director of [Company] (Pty) Ltd, resolve as the first board of directors: (1) The incorporation under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 be finalised; the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation are approved. (2) [Name] hereby subscribes for 100 no-par-value ordinary shares, and the board allots them at R1.00 per share; payment shall be deposited into the company's bank account. (3) The registered office be [Address], South Africa, and the postal address be [Postal Address] as filed with CIPC. (4) [Director] is appointed sole director; [Officer] is appointed chief executive officer; [Secretary] is appointed company secretary. Each accepts office with authority to complete ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services (www.cipc.co.za) or accredited CIPC self-service terminal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the CIPC name database, complete Form CoR 9.1 with a proposed name and two alternatives, pay the statutory reservation fee electronically, and submit. If the name is not reserved, the application proceeds to CIPC's name-refusal procedure.
required_dossiers: Certified identity document or passport of the incorporator
Power of attorney if a registered agent submits
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a Notice of Non-Acceptance, the incorporator must submit an amended Form CoR 9.1 using an accepted alternative name or lodge a formal objection/application for reconsideration within CIPC's prescribed response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI consistent with the Companies Act, prescribe share classes, director powers and quorum rules, and complete Form CoR 14.1. All initial directors must sign consent to act, and the incorporator must sign the incorporation documents. The registered office must fall within South Africa and must be a physical serviceable address, not a post-office box only.
required_dossiers: Registered office and postal address statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC queries are resolved by revising the rejected provision and resubmitting the corrected document through the same filing queue; a cover letter citing the Companies Act section for each deviation should accompany the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in, select company registration, upload the CoR 14.1 and MOI, verify all fields, pay the incorporation filing fee by debit/credit card or electronic funds transfer, and retain the submission reference number. The application is examined against CIPC's automated and manual acceptance criteria.
required_dossiers: Consents to act and identity copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner places the application in abeyance, the electronic filing must be updated and an explanatory memorandum filed; if the 20 business-day rectification period expires, a fresh CoR 14.1 may be filed to preserve eligibility.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation and Company Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor the filing status until approved. Download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and the Notice of Filing with the company's enterprise number. Verify the name, registered office, directors and incorporator details, and open the company's statutory registers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of directors and incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the SLA, lodge a written status query with CIPC's contact centre. If any registered particulars are inaccurate, apply under Companies Act s 26 for rectification of CIPC registration records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an income tax reference number at SARS eFiling using the company registration documents, and register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and Skills Development Levy. Register the company with the Compensation Fund for COIDA risk classification as a manufacturing employer. Obtain a Tax Compliance Status Pin in preparation for procurement and licensing.
required_dossiers: SARS registration forms and employer registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS may request additional financial or source-funding documents; submit them through eFiling. Late registration penalties may be remitted under the Tax Administration Act by filing a notice of objection and application for full/partial remission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Share Capital Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African commercial bank (FIC-licensed accountable institution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the board resolution authorising the account, incorporation documents and beneficial ownership declarations to the chosen bank. Once the account is operational, deposit the agreed subscription price for the issued shares and obtain proof of deposit for the share register.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership declaration under FIC Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank makes further FICA requests, supply the requested source-of-funds/source-of-wealth evidence. If the account is declined, approach another licensed bank or appeal the financial-risk classification through the bank's internal FICA compliance escalation channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Beneficial Ownership and Maintenance of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register portal; company registered office as custodian
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the share register, directors' register and beneficial ownership register. File the Beneficial Ownership Declaration with CIPC, disclosing natural persons who own or control the company's shares, and update the register whenever shareholding changes occur.
required_dossiers: Register of directors and prescribed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A CIPC enforcement notice is cured by filing the outstanding beneficial ownership declaration and paying the late-filing penalty. If the declaration is queried, verify the ultimate natural persons and resubmit with a sworn affidavit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Listed Activity Determination under the EIA Regulations 2014: Basic Assessment (Listing Notice 1) or full Scoping and Environmental Impact Reporting (Listing Notice 2) if the manufacturing operation triggers a listed activity; if no listed activity is triggered, a written/recorded 'no environmental authorisation required' determination is retained on file.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater and trade effluent discharge must comply with the National Water Act 36 of 1998 water-use licence conditions and municipal sewer by-laws; chemical waste storage and solvent residue disposal must meet the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 standards; volatile organic compound and particulate emissions must meet National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 listed-activity and minimum emission standards where applicable, with Occupational Health and Safety Act exposure limits observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the local fire authority; structural load and building compliance certificate by a registered professional engineer; OHS Act workplace registration and compliance clearance; Compensation Fund certificate of good standing under the COIDA; and any municipal land-use consent for industrial manufacturing at the proposed premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling taxpayer portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Pty Ltd must first incorporate through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); upon incorporation, the company is automatically issued an income tax reference number by SARS using CIPC data. Thereafter, apply for VAT registration via eFiling within 21 days of exceeding the compulsory turnover threshold (or immediately upon voluntary registration). Apply for PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy registration if employing staff. A SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin and the company tax certificate are issued after final registration; registration documentation includes COR14.1, directors' identity documents, proof of physical address, and memorandum of incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box classification election is available in South Africa. Statutory elections include: (1) Small Business Corporation status under Section 12E for qualifying private companies whose shareholders are individual natural persons and gross income ≤ ZAR 20 million; (2) Micro Business turnover tax election under Section 48 of the Income Tax Act where turnover ≤ ZAR 1 million; (3) VAT group election under Section 50 of the VAT Act for allowable grouping of domestic VAT vendors; (4) Section 24J elections for debt instruments. Hybrid mismatch rules under Sections 23M-23N of the Income Tax Act are mandatory and not electable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) – Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 mandatory registration threshold on taxable supplies over any 12-month period; ZAR 50,000 voluntary registration threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls. VAT vendors must file returns through SARS eFiling and issue substantive tax invoices; SARS accepts both paper and electronic tax invoices in XML or PDF. SARS is progressively implementing e-invoicing interoperability standards, but there is no API-based real-time clearance requirement at this stage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act if supplied to a non-resident and physically removed from South Africa to a foreign destination by the supplier or on the supplier's instructions in the ordinary course of the sale, with proof of export obtained and retained within 30 days of supply (or extended period approved by SARS). Services are zero-rated under Section 11(2)(l) where supplied to a non-resident and not utilized in South Africa. The zero-rating is unavailable for supplies to SACU residents where the goods are retained in the SACU customs area unless removed further to a non-SACU destination prior to consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) lodged at the South African port of exit
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical movement out of South Africa
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/MT202 confirming foreign payment
Export permit or ITAC license if goods are controlled or restricted
Certificate of Origin (where preferential duty rates are claimed)
Proof of non-resident status of customer (e.g. VAT registration certificate or contractor certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may raise additional assessments within six years for material non-disclosure and without time limit for fraud or misrepresentation; understatement penalties may extend to 200% of the tax shortfall under Section 223 of the Tax Administration Act; interest runs at the prescribed rate from the date the VAT refund is determined to be unpaid. Unsupported or fraudulent zero ratings are subject to full VAT clawback, revised assessments, potential disqualification from VAT registration, and criminal liability for directors under the Tax Administration Act and the Value-Added Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), as the exchange-control authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, with daily administration delegated to authorised dealers (tier-1 commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) operates as a managed-float currency with full current-account convertibility: trade settlements, service fees, royalties, dividends and branch remittances may be paid without prior SARB approval, subject to documentation and reporting through an authorised dealer (AD). Capital-account transactions remain regulated: inward direct investment (equity subscription) is freely receivable through an AD, but foreign shareholder loans, cross-border security, and onward capital transfers may require FinSurv approval or AD-delegated oversight. Profit remittance hurdles are practical: ordinary dividends to non-resident shareholders are permitted without exchange-control approval but attract a 20% Dividends Tax at source; repayment of intercompany loans and exit capital must be traced to inward-funding certificates, CIPC beneficial-ownership filings and FICA-verified source-of-funds documentation. In essence, ZAR is convertible for bona fide current-account purposes, with capital-account flows managed through the AD channel rather than open-ended offshore convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated in full into the South African banking system within 180 days from the earlier of the shipment date or the date of exportation, in accordance with the Currency and Exchanges Act and FinSurv Manuals; extensions are granted only by the authorised dealer for bona fide commercial reasons (e.g., consignment exports or extended payment terms). The mandatory surrender ratio is effectively 100%: every export receipt must be brought into the AD banking channel and either converted to ZAR at the market rate or credited to the exporter's Foreign Currency Account (FCA); there is no partial-conversion tolerance outside the FCA mechanism. The exporter must file the SAD500 customs declaration, retain the commercial invoice, Bill of Lading, proof of payment and bank credit entry, and present these to the AD upon demand; non-compliance triggers FinSurv penalty action, suspension of preferential AD facilities and potential exchange-control offence exposure.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Substantive legal constraints prevent offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex) from acting as the primary bank or authorised dealer for this (Pty) Ltd: they are not appointed ADs under the Exchange Control Regulations, cannot operate South African ZAR clearing, cannot issue FCA accounts, and are not members of the SAMOS RTGS system. Such platforms are treated as third-party payment providers requiring registration under the National Payment System Act, 1998 if they process payments in South Africa; without a local AD partnership, any inbound or outbound ZAR payment is non-compliant. Viability rating for an ISIC 2813 exporter with LC/SWIFT trade rails is LOW-MEDIUM: acceptable as a supplementary collections tool (distributor deposits, small supplier payments routed via SWIFT), provided the EMI's affiliate is licensed in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction and the company maintains the primary operating and FCA relationship with a tier-1 South African bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FICA), the bank must identify all directors, beneficial owners and authorised signatories; a KYC interview (in person or via simultaneous audio-visual session) with at least one executive director or appointed mandate-holder is mandatory before the account is opened for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced manufacturing entity. Remote opening is legally permissible where identity verification is performed by a recognised electronic verification provider (biometric liveness plus RSA ID or foreign-passport verification) and supported by apostilled or certified corporate documents; however, in practice tier-1 South African banks require at least the local directors to attend a physical signing session for the board resolution and bank mandate, while non-resident directors may complete their verification virtually under the bank's FIC-approved remote-onboarding protocol. Defence against onboarding delay: pre-submit the CIPC Beneficial-Ownership register, the Memorandum of Incorporation, foreign shareholder resolutions, source-of-funds evidence and all passport copies before the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident majority ownership and foreign-resident directors without a clear economic substance narrative for a South African manufacturing (Pty) Ltd.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate chart (group organogram), CIPC Beneficial-Ownership register, Memorandum of Incorporation, certified identities of every director and shareholder (passports, visas or residency permits), source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for the subscription monies, tax residency certificates of the immediate foreign shareholder, signed FICA director and UBO verification affidavits, and an economic-substance memorandum explaining the LNG and cryogenic-pump manufacturing programme and funding uses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value exports of cryogenic liquid pumps to non-OECD or sanctions-sensitive end-markets, creating potential dual-use technology or diversion concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory operating licence and ISO 9001 or API-compliant manufacturing certificates, technology classification statement confirming the pumps are commercial LNG infrastructure equipment (not on military or dual-use control lists), export contracts with end-user and end-use attestation, Incoterms and LC terms, denied-party screening reports per counterparty, Bill of Lading and customs export entries (SAD500), and the bank's own sanctions-compliance questionnaire completed with the company's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intercompany and shareholder-loan flows routed via related offshore treasury vehicles in tax-advantaged jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD-compliant transfer-pricing documentation (local file with master file references), executed intercompany agreements with arm's-length pricing, SARB or AD approval or the delegated dealer confirmation for inward shareholder loans (applicable term, interest rate and repayment schedule), FATCA and CRS entity self-certifications, board resolutions authorising each related-party transaction, and tariff or proforma invoices for any cross-border procurement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid round-trip pattern: equity injection, near-term large import prepayments to foreign component suppliers, and remittance of royalties or management fees to the offshore parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 24-month cash-flow and working-capital plan aligned to the LNG pump order book, equity-subscription board resolution and bank statement of the injecting shareholder, supplier proforma invoices, LC (MT700) and SWIFT MT103 or MT202 evidence, the production and freight timeline demonstrating goods actually clear South African customs within the 180-day import window, and the immediate parent's audited financial statements demonstrating repayment capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suppliers or customers domiciled in jurisdictions with no accessible company registry, using virtual addresses or opaque nominee structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate-registry extracts (apostilled where available), supplier bank confirmation of the trade-account, physical-address evidence (lease, utility invoice or notarised occupancy), manufacturer credential pack (catalogue, approved-vendor inspection reports, ISO certificate and plant photos), full beneficial-ownership declaration of the counterparty, and an explanation of how the supplier sits within the global LNG and cryogenic supply chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder's equity subscription must be routed exclusively through a South African authorised dealer: (i) the company passes a board resolution authorising the share issue and opens an inward-capital escrow or operational account; (ii) the shareholder remits USD, EUR or GBP via SWIFT MT103 to that AD account, citing the SARB balance-of-payments purpose code for 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' (inward FDI); (iii) the AD credits the proceeds to the company's Foreign Currency Account or converts to ZAR at the prevailing market rate; (iv) the AD issues a Certificate of Receipt of Inward Funds (the inward-funding certificate) evidencing the original capital contribution - this certificate is the mandatory prerequisite for all future dividend distributions, loan repayments and capital repatriation; (v) where the inward amount exceeds the AD's delegated limits or is combined with a non-resident shareholder loan above the threshold, FinSurv prior approval is required before crediting; and (vi) all subscription monies must be sourced from the shareholder's own bank account, with source-of-funds evidence captured on the FICA file, and the CIPC share register updated before remittance is accepted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for cryogenic-pump component imports and logistics are cleared through the following rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for open-account and supplier payments, executed by the AD only after the company presents the proforma invoice, purchase order, and the SAD500 customs declaration or proof of importation; (ii) commercial irrevocable Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) opened through the AD's trade-finance desk for high-value equipment, with a documentary pack comprising the commercial invoice, insurance certificate, Bill of Lading or airway bill, certificate of origin and inspection certificate; (iii) documentary collections (documents against payment or documents against acceptance) as a secondary rail for established suppliers; (iv) intracompany service and royalty disbursements via MT103 with the relevant BoP service code and transfer-pricing documentation attached; and (v) domestic ZAR legs cleared through SAMOS (South African Multiple Option Settlement) as the national RTGS system. The AD will enforce the 180-day import-settlement rule and may require extended-payment approvals where the supply chain demands longer terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) concluded via a South African authorised dealer for committed foreign-currency trade payables and receivables; settlement is in ZAR on maturity and the underlying exposure must be evidenced by invoices, contracts or L/Cs.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not a permissible primary hedge for a resident (Pty) Ltd in the onshore market because the ZAR is a deliverable currency and offshore NDF books are restricted; equivalent economic cover is available through an onshore FEC with the AD.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) and plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps (CCS) for medium-term and long-term foreign-currency debt or intercompany loan exposures, with the AD or FinSurv approving the underlying capital-account transaction.

Foreign-currency options (European-style) and zero-cost collar structures purchased from an authorised dealer for hedging anticipated import bids on LNG and cryogenic plant and equipment, with maturity matching the tender pipeline.
FEC rollover and early-close facilities at the authorised dealer's prevailing market rates, documented as amendments to the original forward cover contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Form CoR 36.1) including Beneficial Ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; CIPC allowance of 30 business days after the anniversary before late penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of ZAR 180 (~USD 10) per financial year overdue; administrative strike-off after 2 consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) for the annual year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty up to 10% of assessed tax; additional 10% late payment penalty and interest at the prescribed SARS rate on outstanding amounts; criminal liability for wilful non-submission

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more; independent review required if PIS is 100–349; self-review permitted if PIS is below 100. PIS is calculated per Companies Act Regulations 26(2).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs (South African GAAP is fully converged with IFRS)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership register must be submitted with the annual CIPC return; any transfer or acquisition of a beneficial interest must be lodged with CIPC within 7 days of the effective change. Annual confirmation records all current beneficial owners and validates that the register is accurate and up to date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers
Register of Share Capital and share transactions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 (independent review); USD 4,000 - USD 10,000 (full statutory audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Preferential deductions include: Section 12C accelerated capital allowance for new manufacturing machinery (40% first-year allowance on cost; thereafter 20% per annum), Section 11D research and development deduction (150% of qualifying expenditure), and Section 12I industrial policy projects allowance for qualifying greenfield or brownfield investments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Company Income Tax Return; filed via SARS eFiling (https://efiling.sars.gov.za)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the company’s financial year-end, subject to the filed Notice of Assessing Liability. For provisional taxpayers, the provisional return (IRP6) is due semi-annually; final ITR14 is due not later than the day preceding the expiration of 12 months from the year of assessment end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter SARS tax reference number and the financial year-end date (YYYY-MM-DD).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the company’s registration data. No non-resident personal details required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide income from business operations, including export sales and services, before any deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company is a resident, all worldwide income is taxable. No special non-resident entry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempt under s10 of the Income Tax Act, such as qualifying foreign dividends or certain branch income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, exempt income is excluded from the company’s tax base. Attach supporting schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable business deductions under s11(a), including manufacturing costs, depreciation allowances, and trading expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any cross-border payments to related parties must be supported by current transfer pricing documentation to be deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry-forward assessed loss from prior years, restricted to 80% of taxable income after current-year deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward indefinitely; no non-resident-specific rules apply to the company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable income after applying all deductions and assessed loss set-off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company not resident in South Africa, only South African source income would be included; here the entity is a South African resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend withholding tax at 20% on dividends paid to shareholders (or 0% when the beneficial owner is a South African resident company).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must submit the declaration (DTD) and a TRC to apply a reduced treaty rate. Withhold and remit the net amount to SARS on the dividend payment date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file ITR14 on time triggers a monthly administrative non-compliance penalty of ZAR 1,000 (or 25% of assessed tax if greater, capped at ZAR 16,000 per month, depending on taxpayer category), plus an understatement penalty of up to 20% for incorrect returns, and interest at the prescribed rate (currently 10.5% per annum) on outstanding tax from the date payment was due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficial owner must (i) obtain a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, (ii) complete the South African Revenue Service declaration form (DTD – Declaration of Dividend Withholding Tax rate reduction), and (iii) deliver both to the paying company (ZA_PTY_LTD) before the dividend is paid. The paying company must retain the TRC for five years. If the TRC is not provided on time, the statutory 20% rate applies; a refund can be claimed via the IT3D reconciliation or a formal refund application.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalty withholding tax 15% (payments for intellectual property) and interest withholding tax 15% (payments to non-residents for debt). Treaty rates vary by jurisdiction; for example, under the South Africa–UK DTA, royalties are reduced to 0% (patents/copyright) or 12% (other IP); interest is reduced to 0%. A TRC and beneficial ownership declaration must be submitted to the payer before payment to apply the treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File documentation is required when the aggregate value of cross-border affected transactions with connected persons exceeds ZAR 100,000,000 per tax year; Master File is required when the aggregated group cross-border related-party transactions exceed ZAR 1,000,000,000. Below these thresholds, contemporaneous documentation is still recommended to demonstrate arm’s-length pricing and to mitigate penalties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime as found in some offshore jurisdictions. However, the Income Tax Act, common law substance-over-form, and DTA beneficial ownership provisions impose an effective substance requirement. A company must maintain real business activity — such as office premises, payroll, decision-making, and supply-chain involvement — in South Africa. Without economic substance, tax avoidance transaction rules (s80A–s80L) or treaty shopping provisions may disallow benefits, and the company can be treated as a shell resulting in penalties and assessed tax adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting significant income from the ITR14, overstating deductions, or creating fictitious expenses related to cryogenic pump manufacturing or export transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 234 of the Tax Administration Act (No. 28 of 2011), a person convicted of tax evasion is liable to a fine of up to ZAR 10,000,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 10 years. In addition, the full tax underpaid plus 200% understatement penalty may be assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise or collude in tax evasion could face joint and several liability for unpaid tax plus penalties. Criminal conviction can result in direct imprisonment of up to 10 years, travel bans, and disqualification from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using ZA_PTY_LTD as a conduit with no physical office, no employees, and no operational control, solely to route royalty payments or hold South African assets without real substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (s80A–s80L), SARS may disregard the company as a sham and impose a 75% understatement penalty. The company may be assessed as a domestic company on deemed worldwide income, and treaty benefits may be denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for taxes and penalties arising from a re-characterised sham transaction (s80L and s160 of TAA). Personal liability for civil restitution can extend to all amounts unpaid, plus interest. Courts may issue a punitive costs order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using cryogenic pump export/import contracts to over- or under-invoice related parties, matching letters of credit or Swift wire transfers to fictitious trade descriptions, or laundering proceeds through cash-intensive local dealerships without reporting to the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) imposes fines of up to ZAR 100 million or imprisonment up to 15 years for money laundering. The Prevention of Organised Crime Act (POCA) allows asset forfeiture. General banking license infractions can lead to payroll freezing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate or fail to report suspicious transactions face criminal liability, fines, and imprisonment. The corporate veil is pierced under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 (s77) allowing restitution claims against directors for future liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing cross-border sales of cryogenic pumps to a related offshore distributor at a non-arm’s-length margin, failing to maintain Local/Master File, or providing false comparability data to SARS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may adjust the taxable income to an arm’s-length value, impose an additional tax of up to 100% of the adjustment, and levy an understatement penalty of 50% for substantial mispricing. Contemporaneous documentation missing attracts a uniform administrative penalty of up to ZAR 2,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation may be personally liable for the additional tax and penalty if they negligently or knowingly misrepresented facts. Personal liability can lead to sequestration of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring a dividend to a non-resident shareholder without withholding the 20% or without collecting the reduced-rate declaration and TRC, or remitting the amount to SARS late.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company is liable for the unwithheld amount, plus a 10% late payment penalty, and interest at the prescribed rate. In addition, SARS may recover the unpaid amount from the directors as an ordinary debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s143(1) of the Tax Administration Act, directors are jointly and severally liable for the company’s unpaid dividend withholding tax if the company fails to meet its obligation. Civil recovery includes travel bans, attachment of personal bank accounts, and possible contempt of court imprisonment.
